before.name: Planck–Einstein relation
before.description: Relates the energy of a quantum of radiation to its frequency.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Planck–Einstein relation
after.plain: E = h nu = hbar omega
after.description: Relates the energy of a quantum of radiation to its frequency.
assumptions: Single photon or single-mode energy quantum; not the total energy of a multimode state.
variables: E: energy quantum; h: Planck constant; nu: cyclic frequency; hbar=h/(2 pi); omega=2 pi nu.
after.regime: Radiation energy quantum; zero-point energy is not included.
after.units: SI: E in joules, h and hbar in joule seconds, nu in hertz, omega in radians per second.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Photon momentum
before.description: Relates photon momentum to wavelength and wave number.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Photon momentum
after.plain: p = h/lambda = hbar k
after.description: Relates photon momentum to wavelength and wave number.
assumptions: Free photon in vacuum; lambda is vacuum wavelength and p is momentum magnitude.
variables: p: nonnegative photon momentum magnitude; lambda: wavelength; k=2 pi/lambda: wave-number magnitude.
after.regime: Do not apply without qualification to canonical versus kinetic momentum of light inside a material.
after.units: SI: p in kg m/s, lambda in m, k in inverse m.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: de Broglie wavelength
before.description: Associates a wavelength with matter of momentum p.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: de Broglie wavelength
after.plain: lambda = h/p
after.description: Associates a wavelength with matter of momentum p.
assumptions: Momentum eigenmode or locally narrow momentum distribution.
variables: lambda: wavelength; p: magnitude of momentum; h: Planck constant.
after.regime: A localized wave packet generally contains a range of wavelengths; p=0 gives an infinite wavelength limit.
after.units: SI: wavelength in m and momentum in kg m/s.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Time-dependent Schrödinger equation
before.description: Fundamental unitary evolution equation of nonrelativistic wave mechanics.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Time-dependent Schrödinger equation
after.plain: i hbar dPsi/dt = H Psi
after.description: Fundamental unitary evolution equation of nonrelativistic wave mechanics.
assumptions: Closed nonrelativistic quantum system with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian on the relevant state domain.
variables: Psi(r,t): position-space state amplitude; H: Hamiltonian; t: time; hbar: reduced Planck constant.
after.regime: First-order time evolution; for spin or many particles the state and coordinates must be extended. Not a general relativistic field equation.
after.units: H has energy units; both sides have energy times wavefunction units. In 3D single-particle normalization, Psi has units m^(-3/2).
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Time-independent Schrödinger equation
before.description: Stationary-state eigenvalue equation obtained when the Hamiltonian is time independent.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Time-independent Schrödinger equation
after.plain: H psi_n = E_n psi_n
after.description: Stationary-state eigenvalue equation obtained when the Hamiltonian is time independent.
assumptions: Time-independent Hamiltonian; psi_n belongs to its operator domain.
variables: psi_n: energy eigenstate; E_n: corresponding energy eigenvalue; H: Hamiltonian.
after.regime: Spectral eigenvalue problem; continuum eigenstates may require generalized normalization, and the displayed discrete subscript does not imply every spectrum is discrete.
after.units: H and E_n have energy units.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Born probability density
before.description: Gives position probability density from a normalized wavefunction.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Born probability density
after.plain: P = |Psi|^2
after.description: Gives position probability density from a normalized wavefunction.
assumptions: Normalized pure state in a position representation; any internal components must be summed in the norm.
variables: P(r,t): probability density, not probability at one exact point; Psi: wavefunction.
after.regime: Probability for a region is the integral of P over that region.
after.units: For 3D position, P has inverse-volume units and Psi has inverse-square-root-volume units.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Born rule for a projector
before.description: Probability of a projective measurement outcome.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Born rule for a projector
after.plain: p(a) = <psi|P_a|psi>
after.description: Probability of a projective measurement outcome.
assumptions: Normalized pure state and orthogonal projector P_a=P_a dagger=P_a squared for the measurement event.
variables: psi: unit state vector; P_a: projector onto the event subspace; p(a): outcome probability.
after.regime: Projective measurement, including degenerate eigenspaces; a general measurement uses positive POVM effects rather than necessarily projectors.
after.units: p(a) and the projector are dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Born rule in density-operator form
before.description: General probability rule for a POVM effect E_a.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Born rule in density-operator form
after.plain: p(a) = Tr(rho E_a)
after.description: General probability rule for a POVM effect E_a.
assumptions: rho is positive, trace one; each E_a is a positive measurement effect and the effects sum to identity.
variables: rho: density operator; E_a: POVM effect; p(a): event probability.
after.regime: Applies to pure or mixed states and generalized measurements; the effect does not alone determine the post-measurement state.
after.units: All quantities are dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Expectation value
before.description: Expected measurement value of an observable.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Expectation value
after.plain: <A> = <psi|A|psi> = Tr(rho A)
after.description: Expected measurement value of an observable.
assumptions: Normalized pure state for the bra-ket expression; rho positive and trace one for the trace expression.
The observable is self-adjoint and the state has a finite expectation on its appropriate domain.
variables: A: observable; rho: density operator; psi: state; angle brackets: ensemble expectation.
after.regime: The pure-state and density-operator expressions agree when rho is the pure-state projector; an expectation need not be an eigenvalue observed in one trial.
after.units: The expectation has the same units as A.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Wavefunction normalization
before.description: Normalization condition for a pure-state wavefunction.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Wavefunction normalization
after.plain: integral |Psi|^2 d^3r = 1
after.description: Normalization condition for a pure-state wavefunction.
assumptions: Square-integrable single-particle wavefunction on all 3D position space; include internal-state norm if present.
variables: Psi(r,t): wavefunction; d^3r: position-volume element.
after.regime: Not ordinary normalization of ideal position or momentum eigenkets, which use delta-function normalization.
after.units: Psi has units length^(-3/2); the integral is dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Canonical commutation relation
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Canonical commutation relation
after.plain: [x,p] = i hbar
after.description: Canonical position–momentum commutator.
assumptions: Cartesian position and its canonical conjugate momentum on a common suitable dense domain.
variables: x: one coordinate operator; p: its canonical momentum; i: imaginary unit; hbar: reduced Planck constant.
after.regime: For multiple Cartesian coordinates, [x_i,p_j]=i hbar delta_ij; this is not the algebra of arbitrary angular or compact coordinates.
after.units: Both sides have action units.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Commutator definition
before.latex: [\hat A,\hat B]=\hat A\hat B-\hat B\hat A
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Commutator definition
after.latex: [\hat A,\hat B]=\hat A\hat B-\hat B\hat A
after.plain: [A,B] = AB-BA
after.description: Defines the operator commutator.
assumptions: The products AB and BA are defined on the common domain of interest.
variables: A,B: linear operators; [A,B]: their commutator.
after.regime: Algebraic definition, not an independent dynamical law.
after.units: Commutator units are the product of the units of A and B.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Position–momentum uncertainty
before.description: Special case of the uncertainty principle for canonical position and momentum.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Position–momentum uncertainty
after.plain: Delta x Delta p >= hbar/2
after.description: Special case of the uncertainty principle for canonical position and momentum.
assumptions: Canonical x and p with finite variances and sufficient common-domain regularity.
variables: Delta x and Delta p: standard deviations in the same quantum state, not instrumental errors.
after.regime: State-preparation variance bound; it is not a general measurement-disturbance relation.
after.units: The product has action units.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: Unitary time evolution
before.description: Time evolution for a time-independent Hamiltonian.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Unitary time evolution
after.plain: psi(t)=U psi(t0)
after.description: Time evolution for a time-independent Hamiltonian.
assumptions: Closed-system evolution generated by a self-adjoint time-independent Hamiltonian for the displayed exponential.
variables: U(t,t0): unitary propagator; H: Hamiltonian; t0: initial time; psi: state vector.
after.regime: For noncommuting Hamiltonians at different times, replace the simple exponential by the time-ordered propagator.
after.units: H(t-t0)/hbar is dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

before.name: von Neumann equation
before.description: Unitary evolution equation for a density operator.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: von Neumann equation
after.plain: i hbar drho/dt = [H,rho]
after.description: Unitary evolution equation for a density operator.
assumptions: Closed-system unitary evolution, or the full system including environment; H is self-adjoint.
variables: rho: density operator; H: Hamiltonian; [H,rho]: commutator.
after.regime: Not a generic reduced open-system equation: tracing out an environment may introduce dissipative and memory terms.
after.units: Both sides have energy units because rho is dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical representative

after.name: Abelian Higgs linearized vector mass
after.plain: The linearized Abelian gauge field has mass squared equal to e squared times the scalar vacuum amplitude squared.
after.description: The original Abelian example exhibits a massive vector mode after expanding about a symmetry-breaking scalar vacuum. This is not the full electroweak mass formula.
assumptions: Four-dimensional flat spacetime with metric signature (-,+,+,+).
Two real scalar fields with potential V(phi_1^2+phi_2^2), vacuum phi_1=0 and phi_2=phi_0 nonzero, V prime(phi_0^2)=0 and V double-prime(phi_0^2)>0.
Retain terms linear in scalar and vector perturbations; classical/tree-level bare mass, not a radiatively corrected pole mass.
variables: B_mu = A_mu - partial_mu(delta phi_1)/(e phi_0): gauge-invariant linearized vector variable.
G_mu_nu = partial_mu B_nu - partial_nu B_mu: vector field strength.
e: dimensionless Abelian gauge coupling; phi_0: scalar vacuum amplitude; m_B: nonnegative bare vector mass.
after.regime: Small fluctuations around a stable nonzero Abelian scalar vacuum with e phi_0 nonzero; the B-variable definition is singular at e phi_0=0, although the original field equations have a massless decoupling limit.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1. B_mu, phi_0 and m_B have mass dimension 1; partial_mu has mass dimension 1; G_mu_nu has mass dimension 2.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative linearized realization of the mechanism; not a claim that all gauge bosons acquire mass or that this Abelian model is the Standard Model.

sourceLocations.locator: PRL 13 (1964), printed p. 508 (PDF page 1): Eq. (3) defines B and G; Eq. (4) gives the transverse massive-vector equation; immediately following text identifies bare mass e phi_0. Equation (1) and surrounding text fix the metric and vacuum assumptions.

after.name: Four-function Horndeski action
after.plain: Four free functions of a scalar field and its kinetic invariant combine curvature and scalar derivatives so that the field equations remain second order.
after.description: The generalized-Galileon form of the four-dimensional Horndeski scalar–metric action, equivalent to the original formulation up to integrations by parts. It defines a family rather than one phenomenological model.
assumptions: Four-dimensional local scalar–metric theory with one scalar and a torsion-free Levi-Civita connection.
X=-g^{mu nu}(partial_mu phi)(partial_nu phi)/2; every K and G_i is a function of (phi,X).
Boundary terms are neglected under suitable boundary conditions; second-order equations do not by themselves guarantee stability or observational viability.
variables: g_mu_nu: spacetime metric with signature (-,+,+,+); g: its determinant; R: Ricci scalar; G_mu_nu: Einstein tensor.
phi: scalar field; X: kinetic invariant; Box phi = g^{mu nu} nabla_mu nabla_nu phi.
G_iX = partial G_i / partial X; K,G_3,G_4,G_5: arbitrary sufficiently differentiable functions.
(nabla nabla phi)^2 = nabla_mu nabla_nu phi nabla^mu nabla^nu phi; the cubic abbreviation denotes the cyclic contraction nabla_mu nabla_nu phi nabla^nu nabla^lambda phi nabla_lambda nabla^mu phi.
after.regime: Classical covariant single-scalar metric theory. Includes GR with a minimally coupled canonical scalar for K=X-V, G_3=G_5=0, G_4=M_Pl^2/2; excludes beyond-Horndeski/DHOST extensions with higher-order equations.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1. With scalar mass dimension 1, X has dimension 4, K dimension 4, G_3 dimension 1, G_4 dimension 2 and G_5 dimension -1, so every L_i has dimension 4 and S is dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: Defining representative form of the Horndeski family; no inflationary background, screening solution, stability condition, or observational constraint is imposed by this action alone.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1105.5723v4, section 2, Eq. (2.1)–(2.2) printed/PDF p. 2 and Eq. (2.3)–(2.5) printed/PDF p. 3; Appendix A establishes equivalence with Horndeski.

after.name: Original Kobayashi–Maskawa mixing matrix
after.plain: A unitary three-generation quark mixing matrix contains three rotation angles and one phase that can generate CP violation.
after.description: The original KM parametrization, using the corrected Eq. (13) printed in the source erratum. Its angle and phase conventions are not the later standard PDG convention.
assumptions: Exactly three up-type and three down-type quarks, with unitary mixing among them in the charged weak current.
Unphysical quark-field rephasings have been removed; theta_1, theta_2, theta_3 and delta are real.
A complex phase alone is not sufficient for observable CP violation in all limits: vanishing mixing angles or appropriate mass degeneracies can remove its physical effect.
variables: V_KM: dimensionless quark mixing matrix in the original Kobayashi–Maskawa convention.
theta_i: three mixing angles; c_i and s_i: their cosines and sines; delta: CP phase in this convention.
Rows and columns label up-type and down-type mass eigenstates respectively; generation naming is modern rather than the source six-plet notation.
after.regime: Three-generation charged-current quark mixing. Additional quarks can make an observed 3 by 3 submatrix nonunitary; this formula does not cover such extensions.
after.units: Every matrix entry and angle is dimensionless; angles are in radians.
after.theoryRelationship: An explicit parametrization of the unitary mixing structure, not an independent dynamical equation or a numerical fit.

sourceLocations.locator: Progress of Theoretical Physics 49 (1973), printed p. 657, PDF page 6: corrected Eq. (13) in the Errata block at the bottom of the page. The uncorrected main-text matrix has typographical errors and is not used.

after.name: Type-I seesaw effective light-neutrino mass
after.plain: Integrating out heavy singlet Majorana neutrinos generates a suppressed light-neutrino mass matrix.
after.description: Leading tree-level type-I seesaw relation, with the transpose rather than Hermitian conjugate required for the symmetric Majorana mass matrix.
assumptions: No direct left-handed Majorana mass term, as in the minimal model without a scalar triplet.
Invertible symmetric heavy Majorana mass matrix M_R, with heavy–light mixing norm ||m_D M_R^{-1}|| much smaller than one.
Tree-level matching below heavy-neutrino thresholds; radiative corrections and higher-order heavy–light mixing are neglected.
variables: m_nu: complex symmetric effective light-neutrino Majorana mass matrix (m_L in the cited paper).
m_D: Dirac mass matrix, with active-flavour index on rows and heavy-singlet index on columns.
M_R: symmetric heavy-singlet Majorana mass matrix; superscript T denotes transpose, not complex conjugation.
after.regime: Minimal type-I hierarchy. Not the inverse/type-II/type-III seesaw, and not an exact formula for arbitrary heavy–light mixing.
after.units: All three mass matrices have mass dimension 1 in hbar=c=1 units.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative leading effective mass relation. The cited paper makes additional flavour assumptions for its phenomenology, but its hierarchical Dirac spectrum and alignment are not required for this general matching formula.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:hep-ph/0001041v1, printed/PDF p. 1, Introduction, Eq. (1), with m_L renamed m_nu. Approximate equality makes explicit the leading seesaw expansion; the paper prints equality for its effective mass matrix.

after.name: Landau quasiparticle energy variation
after.plain: A small occupation change shifts quasiparticle energies through the Landau interaction function.
after.description: Linear response of quasiparticle energy to the occupation distribution. The spin trace is kept in the original operator form; f is a quasiparticle interaction, not a microscopic bare interaction.
assumptions: Normal, non-superfluid Fermi liquid with well-defined quasiparticles near the Fermi surface.
Small changes in occupations; interaction function is evaluated in the reference state.
variables: delta epsilon(p): quasiparticle energy change, an operator in the untraced spin indices.
f(p,p prime): Landau interaction function with spin indices implicit; delta n(p prime): change of the quasiparticle occupation matrix.
Tr_sigma_prime: trace over the second quasiparticle spin indices.
after.regime: Low-energy normal Fermi-liquid response; not valid as a quasiparticle description in generic one-dimensional Luttinger liquids or across a superfluid gap.
after.units: Source uses hbar=1 and d tau=d^3p/(2 pi)^3. Restoring hbar replaces the denominator by (2 pi hbar)^3; f has dimensions energy times volume, so the integral is an energy.
after.theoryRelationship: Defining phenomenological interaction response, not a theorem that every interacting Fermi system is a Fermi liquid.

sourceLocations.locator: Soviet Physics JETP 8 (1959), printed p. 70, PDF page 1, Eq. (1) and the following measure definition d tau=d^3p/(2 pi)^3, hbar=1. Sp_sigma_prime is rewritten as Tr_sigma_prime.

after.name: Nakajima–Zwanzig projected memory equation
after.latex: \frac{d}{dt}\mathcal P\rho(t)=\int_0^t ds\,\mathcal K(t,s)\mathcal P\rho(s),\qquad\mathcal K(t,s)=\mathcal P\mathcal L(t)\mathcal T\exp\!\left[\int_s^t du\,\mathcal Q\mathcal L(u)\right]\mathcal Q\mathcal L(s)\mathcal P
after.plain: The projected state evolves through a memory kernel integrating its history.
after.description: Exact homogeneous interaction-picture equation under the stated projection and initial-state conditions; not its second-order truncation.
assumptions: Fixed projection P squared=P; Q=I-P.
P rho(0)=rho(0) and P L(t) P=0; otherwise initial-correlation and instantaneous projected terms must be retained.
variables: rho: full density operator; P: relevant-state projection; Q: complementary projection.
L(t)A=-i[H_I(t),A] in hbar=1 units; T: chronological ordering; K: memory superoperator.
after.regime: Exact before approximating the kernel. A factorizing projection requires a compatible initially uncorrelated state for the homogeneous form.
after.units: hbar=1; L has inverse-time units and K inverse-time-squared units.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative exact projection identity, distinct from a Born or Markov approximation.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:0708.0410v2, printed/PDF p.2, section II.B, Eqs.(2)–(5) and initial-state caveat following Eq.(4).

after.name: Two-flavour matter mixing and MSW resonance
after.latex: A=\frac{\Delta m^2}{4E}\cos2\theta_v-\frac{G_F N_e}{\sqrt2},\quad B=\frac{\Delta m^2}{4E}\sin2\theta_v,\quad\sin^2(2\theta_m)=\frac{B^2}{A^2+B^2},\quad A_{\rm res}=0
after.plain: Matter modifies the mixing angle; the resonance is maximal effective mixing when the diagonal splitting vanishes and the off-diagonal mixing remains nonzero.
after.description: Instantaneous two-active-flavour mixing for electron-neutrino conversion to a muon or tau flavour combination. This local resonance condition is not by itself a full conversion-probability formula.
assumptions: Ultrarelativistic coherent two-flavour propagation with standard weak forward scattering in ordinary unpolarized matter.
The common identity part of the flavour Hamiltonian has been removed; its remaining matrix is [[-A,B],[B,A]].
N_e is electron number density; for antineutrinos change N_e to -N_e. Resonant mixing requires B nonzero and a physically attainable density.
variables: Delta m^2=m_2^2-m_1^2: signed vacuum splitting; E: neutrino energy; theta_v: vacuum mixing angle; theta_m: local matter mixing angle.
G_F: Fermi constant; N_e: electron number density; A,B: Hamiltonian coefficients with energy units.
after.regime: Local two-active-flavour reduction. Nonadiabatic profiles require solving the propagation equation; sterile channels have different effective densities, and genuine three-flavour effects are not included.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1: G_F has mass dimension -2 and N_e dimension 3, so A,B have dimension 1; mixing-angle expressions are dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative matter-mixing relation, distinct from the additional adiabatic-following assumptions needed for the usual solar MSW conversion picture.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:hep-ph/9805272v3, printed/PDF p.3 Eqs.(1)–(3), p.4 Eq.(4) and immediately following resonance statement. Squared mixing-angle form is the algebraic square of Eq.(4); select N=N_e from Eq.(3).

after.name: Nonsecular single-channel Redfield equation
after.plain: A bath-filtered system operator determines weak-coupling dissipation without imposing a secular approximation.
after.description: The asymptotic-coefficient Redfield generator in a one-Hermitian-channel convention. This is the source Redfield equation, not the paper’s proposed completely positive GAME modification.
assumptions: H_tot=H_0+H_B+A tensor B with Hermitian coupling operators; take the bath mean of B to vanish or absorb it into H_0.
Born weak-coupling and short bath-correlation-time Markov approximation; bath remains in a stationary thermal state.
Integrals are extended to infinity; no secular approximation is imposed.
variables: rho: reduced system density operator in the Schrodinger picture; H_0: system Hamiltonian.
A(-tau)=exp(-i H_0 tau) A exp(i H_0 tau); A_f: bath-filtered operator.
C(t)=Tr_B[rho_B B(t)B(0)]: stationary bath correlation; B(t)=exp(i H_B t)B exp(-i H_B t).
after.regime: Weak-coupling Markov regime; nonsecular Redfield evolution need not preserve positivity or complete positivity, especially outside its validity regime.
after.units: hbar=1. Choose A dimensionless and B with energy units; C has energy squared units, A_f energy units, and every right-hand term inverse-time units.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative approximate generator, not a universal exact open-system evolution law and not automatically of Lindblad form.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:2003.09063v4, printed/PDF p.3, section2 Eq.(1) and bath-correlation paragraph; section3 Eqs.(4)–(5) for the Redfield generator and A_f.

after.name: Caldeira–Leggett oscillator-bath Hamiltonian
after.plain: A system coordinate couples linearly to harmonic bath oscillators, with the potential counterterm retained.
after.description: Coordinate-coupled Brownian specialization of the oscillator-bath model. Completing the square makes the counterterm convention explicit.
assumptions: Canonical system and bath coordinate–momentum pairs; positive bath masses and frequencies.
Choose a single bath and system coupling V=q. The displayed U is the potential before bath-induced static renormalization; the counterterm cancels that shift.
variables: q,p,M,U: system coordinate, momentum, mass and potential.
x_j,p_j,m_j,omega_j: bath oscillator coordinates, momenta, masses and angular frequencies; c_j: bilinear coupling constants.
after.regime: A defining microscopic model. A dissipative continuum limit needs a specified spectral density and initial bath state; the high-temperature Markov master equation requires additional approximations.
after.units: SI: q,x_j in m, masses in kg, frequencies in s^(-1), c_j in kg/s^2; every Hamiltonian term is an energy.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative linear-coordinate oscillator-bath model, not the Caldeira–Leggett approximate master equation.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:2006.05501v2, printed/PDF pp.2–3: section II Eqs.(1)–(2), with the Brownian specialization and explicit counterterm in the paragraph beginning “A notable example”. Complete the oscillator square and set one bath with V=q.

after.name: Drude-bath infinite HEOM hierarchy
after.latex: \dot\rho_{\mathbf n}=-i[H_S,\rho_{\mathbf n}]-\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}n_k\nu_k\rho_{\mathbf n}-i\left[V,\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\rho_{\mathbf n+\mathbf e_k}\right]-i\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}n_k\left(c_kV\rho_{\mathbf n-\mathbf e_k}-c_k^*\rho_{\mathbf n-\mathbf e_k}V\right)
after.plain: Auxiliary density operators couple neighboring tiers to retain Gaussian bath memory.
after.description: Unscaled infinite hierarchy for a single Drude oscillator bath, rewriting the source separate Drude and Matsubara indices as one multi-index and using hbar=1. No finite cutoff correction is present in this infinite limit.
assumptions: H_tot=H_S+H_B−V sum_j alpha_j x_j with Hermitian V; Gaussian harmonic bath at inverse temperature beta.
Source spectral convention J(omega)=eta gamma^2 omega/[pi(gamma^2+omega^2)].

Infinite exponential expansion and untruncated hierarchy. A numerical implementation must establish convergence in both Matsubara terms and hierarchy depth; finite cutoffs are not automatically exact.
variables: rho_0: physical reduced density operator; rho_n: unscaled auxiliary operators; n_k: nonnegative tier occupations; e_k: unit multi-index.
nu_0=gamma; nu_k=2 pi k/beta for k>=1; gamma: bath decay rate.

c_0=(eta gamma^2/2)[cot(beta gamma/2)−i]; c_k=2 eta gamma^2 nu_k/[beta(nu_k^2−gamma^2)] for k>=1. At coincident poles, take the combined analytic limit rather than evaluate divergent pieces separately.
H_S: system Hamiltonian; V: dimensionless coupling operator; eta: bath coupling parameter; beta=1/(k_B T).
after.regime: Gaussian Drude environment without Born, Markov or secular truncation. Factorized initial states use zero higher ADOs; correlated preparation requires compatible nonzero initial ADOs.
after.units: hbar=1, dimensionless V and eta. H_S,gamma,nu_k have energy dimension1; c_k dimension2. In this unscaled convention a tier-N ADO has energy dimension N, so every term has dimension N+1.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative exact infinite hierarchy for the specified bath, not every HEOM decomposition or a guarantee for a finite numerical truncation.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1407.1811v2, Eq.(40) printed/PDF p.14; relaxation definitions Eqs.(33),(35),(37) p.13 and Drude correlation coefficients earlier in section III. Set hbar=1, K→infinity so Xi→0, combine the source n and j_k into n_0,n_k, and combine commutator/anticommutator lowering terms using complex c_0.

after.name: Static Ginzburg–Landau order-parameter equation
after.plain: The superconducting order parameter balances gradient, quadratic and quartic free-energy terms.
after.description: Isotropic static specialization of the review anisotropic Ginzburg–Landau equation, using Gaussian electromagnetic units and a positive pair-charge magnitude.
assumptions: Local single-component order parameter close enough to a continuous transition for a quartic gradient expansion; beta>0.
Isotropic effective mass m_*; Gaussian electromagnetic convention, e_*>0 is the pair-charge magnitude, physical Cooper-pair charge −e_*.
Static extremum with suitable boundary conditions; magnetic response additionally requires Maxwell/supercurrent equation.
variables: Psi: order parameter, normalized so |Psi|^2 is pair density; alpha: quadratic coefficient, negative in the uniform superconducting phase; beta: quartic coefficient.
m_*: pair effective mass; e_*: pair-charge magnitude; A: vector potential; c: speed of light.
after.regime: Mesoscopic mean-field/phenomenological static GL model near T_c; not a microscopic pairing theory or a time-dependent equation.
after.units: Gaussian electromagnetic units. Psi has dimension length^(-3/2), alpha energy, beta energy times volume; e_* A/c has momentum units.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative equilibrium equation from varying a GL free energy, with source a prime renamed alpha and b prime renamed beta; not a claim that all superconductors have a scalar isotropic order parameter.

sourceLocations.locator: Author preprint arXiv:0905.4224v1, printed/PDF p.4, Eqs.(7),(9),(10), setting m_c*=m* and combining planar/z derivatives. Gaussian flux convention Phi_0=hc/e_* appears Eq.(1), p.2. Coefficients renamed to avoid conflating source beta-like notation with inverse temperature.

after.name: TEGR curvature–torsion boundary identity
after.plain: The torsion scalar reproduces the Einstein–Hilbert action up to a divergence in metric teleparallel geometry.
after.description: The metric-teleparallel identity and TEGR gravitational action in the cited review sign convention. The over-ring denotes the Levi-Civita connection, not the flat teleparallel connection.
assumptions: Four-dimensional metric-compatible teleparallel connection with vanishing curvature and generally nonzero torsion.
Review signature (+,−,−,−), with connection last index the differentiation index and T^rho_mu_nu=Gamma^rho_nu_mu−Gamma^rho_mu_nu.
Appropriate boundary treatment when comparing actions; boundary terms cannot simply be discarded in all variational or charge calculations.
variables: R with over-ring: Levi-Civita Ricci scalar; T^rho_mu_nu: teleparallel torsion; T: scalar defined as S_rho^mu_nu T^rho_mu_nu/2 using review Eq.(1.6).
S_rho^mu_nu=K^mu_nu_rho−delta_rho^mu T_sigma^sigma_nu+delta_rho^nu T_sigma^sigma_mu; K: contortion, teleparallel minus Levi-Civita connection.
kappa^2=8 pi G in c=1 units; g: metric determinant.
after.regime: Classical TEGR equivalence for the metric equations. Replacing T by a nonlinear f(T) generally breaks the simple equivalence, and symmetric teleparallel gravity uses nonmetricity Q instead.
after.units: hbar=c=1: R and T have mass dimension2, kappa^2 dimension−2, and the gravitational action is dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: Geometric identity plus representative TEGR action; not an empirical demonstration of torsion or a formula for every teleparallel modification.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:2106.13793v4, printed p.18 / PDF p.25, Eqs.(2.49),(2.51),(2.52); signature and connection conventions printed pp.6–7 / PDF pp.13–14; torsion/contortion/superpotential/scalar Eq.(1.6), printed p.7 / PDF p.14.

after.name: Brans–Dicke trace-sourced scalar equation
after.plain: The matter stress-energy trace sources the Brans–Dicke scalar.
after.description: Potential-free Brans–Dicke representative within the broader scalar–tensor family.
assumptions: Constant dimensionless omega, 3+2 omega nonzero; no scalar potential.
Matter minimally couples to the Jordan-frame metric, not explicitly to phi.
Signature (−,+,+,+); torsion-free metric connection.
variables: phi: inverse-gravitational-coupling scalar; omega: Brans–Dicke parameter.
Box phi = nabla_mu nabla^mu phi; T=g_mu_nu T^mu_nu, equal to −energy density+3 pressure for a perfect fluid.
after.regime: Classical potential-free Brans–Dicke model; not every scalar–tensor theory. Traceless matter has no direct source here, but boundary conditions can still support scalar variation.
after.units: SI: phi has inverse-G units kg s^2/m^3; T has energy-density units; coordinates use x^0=ct.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative field equation, not a universal scalar–tensor identity.

sourceLocations.locator: Physical Review124(1961), printed p.930/PDFp.6, Eq.(13); d’Alembertian Eq.(10),p.929; perfect-fluid trace Eqs.(14)–(15),p.930.

after.name: Two-generation GIM flavour-diagonal neutral current
after.plain: Orthogonal mixing of two complete quark generations makes the weak neutral-current generator diagonal in flavour.
after.description: The historical four-quark construction exhibits absence of tree-level flavour-changing neutral currents; it does not assert vanishing loop amplitudes for unequal quark masses.
assumptions: Historical two-generation real Cabibbo mixing with complete (u,d) and (c,s) weak doublets.
The block matrix uses the source ordering (u,c,d,s); C acts on the left-chiral flavour space.
No CP-violating phase in this two-generation construction; transpose and adjoint agree for U.
variables: theta: Cabibbo angle; U: real orthogonal 2 by 2 charged-current mixing matrix.
C: dimensionless weak raising generator in the four-quark flavour space; dagger: Hermitian conjugation; I_2: identity.
after.regime: Tree-level weak-isospin structure of the historical four-quark model. Higher-order FCNC can survive mass splitting; this is not a three-generation loop-rate formula.
after.units: All matrices and angles are dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative algebraic basis for GIM suppression, not a numerical rare-decay prediction.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1303.6154v1, PDF p.5 Section 4 Eqs.(14)–(16); explicit I_2 notation replaces the source block identity symbol 1. PDF pp.4–5 explains equal-mass loop cancellation separately.

after.name: Luttinger phase-density Hamiltonian
after.plain: Long-wavelength phase gradients and density fluctuations form a quadratic sound-mode theory.
after.description: Single-chain Hamiltonian from the source coupled-chain setup, before adding interchain tunnelling. The source distinguishes the single-chain parameter script K from the antisymmetric-sector parameter K=script K/2.
assumptions: Low-energy, long-wavelength gapless one-dimensional bosonic fluid; stable positive u and script K.
n_alpha is the fluctuation of linear number density, not total density.
This is the isolated-chain quadratic term, not the full sine-Gordon Hamiltonian with tunnelling.
variables: u: sound velocity; script K: dimensionless single-chain Luttinger parameter; hbar: reduced Planck constant.
theta_alpha: dimensionless phase; n_alpha: density fluctuation with inverse-length units; x: chain coordinate; alpha,beta: chain labels.
after.regime: Continuum hydrodynamic regime below the microscopic cutoff. Irrelevant nonlinear terms, commensurate gaps, and interchain coupling are not part of this displayed Hamiltonian.
after.units: SI-compatible with explicit hbar: hbar u has energy times length; integral of squared gradients or densities has inverse length, yielding energy.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative bosonic realization of Luttinger-liquid theory; does not equate the microscopic interaction with the phenomenological Luttinger parameter.

sourceLocations.locator: Physical Review A 91, 023627 (2015), printed p.023627-2 / PDF p.2 Eq.(2) and following canonical-commutator paragraph. Gradient rewritten as partial_x in one dimension.

after.name: BKT universal stiffness jump
after.plain: The thermodynamic stiffness immediately below vortex unbinding has a universal ratio to temperature.
after.description: Nelson–Kosterlitz jump expressed with an energy-valued renormalized phase stiffness, not a three-dimensional mass density.
assumptions: Two-dimensional short-range XY / U(1) phase model in the BKT universality class with logarithmic vortex interactions.
J_s is the long-distance renormalized helicity modulus in the thermodynamic limit, not the bare microscopic coupling.
Use the low-temperature-side limit; finite samples require finite-size corrections.
variables: J_s: energy-valued two-dimensional superfluid phase stiffness
T_BKT: transition temperature
k_B: Boltzmann constant.
after.regime: Thermodynamic BKT critical point. Finite size, non-BKT interactions, and experimental rounding do not obey this as an exact finite-sample crossing rule.
after.units: J_s and k_B T both have energy units. Source sets k_B=1.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative universal consequence of vortex unbinding, not a formula for T_BKT from a bare coupling alone.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1802.03315v1, PDF p.2 Eq.(3), repeated p.4 Eq.(8); p.4 Eq.(9) distinguishes finite-size stiffness from its thermodynamic limit. k_B is restored from the source temperature-as-energy convention; minus specifies the ordered-side limit.

after.name: Single-impurity Anderson Hamiltonian
after.latex: H_{\rm AM}=\sum_\sigma\epsilon_d d_\sigma^\dagger d_\sigma+U n_{d\uparrow}n_{d\downarrow}+\sum_{k\sigma}\epsilon_{k\sigma}c_{k\sigma}^\dagger c_{k\sigma}+\sum_{k\sigma}(V_kd_\sigma^\dagger c_{k\sigma}+V_k^*c_{k\sigma}^\dagger d_\sigma)
after.plain: A correlated localized orbital exchanges electrons with a noninteracting conduction bath.
after.description: The bare single-orbital Anderson model balances hybridization and local double-occupancy repulsion. This is not the source renormalized quasiparticle Hamiltonian.
assumptions: One localized spin-degenerate orbital with local interaction U, coupled by spin-conserving hopping to a noninteracting bath.
Operators obey canonical fermion anticommutation and n_dsigma=d_sigma dagger d_sigma.
No wide-flat-band approximation is needed for this Hamiltonian; the source imposes it only for constant hybridization width.
variables: d_sigma: impurity electron annihilation operator; c_ksigma: bath electron annihilation operator; sigma: spin; k: bath mode.
epsilon_d, epsilon_ksigma: orbital energies relative to a common reference; U: on-site interaction energy; V_k: complex hybridization amplitude.
after.regime: Single-orbital quantum impurity model, including mixed-valence and local-moment regimes. Additional orbitals, bath interactions, phonons, or explicit bias require extensions.
after.units: All epsilon, U and V parameters have energy units; mode operators and occupancies are dimensionless.
after.theoryRelationship: Defining representative model Hamiltonian; displaying it is not an exact solution or an assertion that every parameter choice is in the Kondo regime.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:cond-mat/0312484v2, PDF p.1 Section 1 Eq.(1) and immediately adjacent definitions; distinguish the later renormalized Eq.(4).

after.plain: Energy-momentum sources curvature, while intrinsic spin sources algebraic torsion.
after.description: Sciama–Kibble equations in Trautman’s metric-compatible Riemann–Cartan conventions and geometrized units. The curvature is that of the full connection, not the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection.
assumptions: Four-dimensional classical metric-compatible Einstein–Cartan theory with matter energy-momentum and intrinsic spin.
Follow the source metric signature (1,3), torsion convention Q^rho_munu=Gamma^rho_munu-Gamma^rho_numu in a holonomic frame, and source curvature convention.
The Hilbert-type gravity action yields algebraic torsion; no additional propagating-torsion kinetic terms are included.
variables: g_munu: metric; R_munu,R: Ricci tensor and scalar of the full metric-compatible connection; t_munu: generally asymmetric energy-momentum tensor.
Q^rho_munu: torsion tensor; s^rho_munu: intrinsic spin density in the source index order; delta: Kronecker tensor.
after.regime: Classical Einstein–Cartan field theory. Spin-free regions have vanishing torsion in this minimal theory; no quantum-gravity completion or observational confirmation of torsion follows.
after.units: Source geometrized units G=c=1, with mass and energy measured as length and hbar having length squared. In length-valued coordinates curvature and t have inverse-length-squared units; torsion and spin density have inverse-length units.
after.theoryRelationship: Representative classical extension of general relativity coupling intrinsic spin to torsion, not a quantization of gravity.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:gr-qc/0606062v1, PDF p.5 Eqs.(23)–(24); p.1 Notation gives G=c=1 and signature (1,3); p.3 defines torsion and curvature; p.4 imposes metricity before Eq.(22).
